bihar_raw_news.title: India Infrastructure Projects Face ₹3.40 Lakh Crore Cost Overrun - The Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: August 26, 2026 Govt infrastructure projects see cost overrun of Rs 3.4 lakh crore Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Infrastructure projects worth more than Rs 150 crore each recorded a cumulative cost overrun of around Rs 3,40,504 crore, according to a monthly Government report for July 2026. A total of 1,775 ongoing infrastructure projects across 17 Central Ministries/ Departments were monitored, and it was found that the total revised cost was Rs 37,10,642 crore compared to their original cost of Rs 33,70,138 crore. The report, however, did not specify the actual number of projects that faced cost overrun. The cumulative expenditure incurred on these projects stands at `19.26 lakh crore, accounting for approximately 51.91 per cent of the revised project cost, indicating steady progress in project implementation, a statement by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) said. A significant proportion of projects are at advanced stages, with 675 projects (38 per cent) achieving over 80 per cent physical progress, while 305 (17 per cent) have crossed 80 per cent financial completion. The data also reflects a balanced pipeline, with projects distributed across early and advanced stages of implementation. The Transport & Logistics sector accounts for the highest number of ongoing projects (1,246 projects), with revised estimates of Rs 19.81 lakh crore underscoring priority to connectivity-driven infrastructure growth. 1,775 ongoing infrastructure projects include 735 Mega projects (project cost of Rs 1,000 crore & above) with an original cost of Rs 28.77 lakh crore, and 1,040 Major projects (project cost below Rs 1,000 crore and up to Rs 150 crore) amounting to Rs 4.93 lakh crore. Physical and financial progress broadly move in tandem, with a large number of projects clustered at the initial (0–20 per cent) and advanced (81–100 per cent) stages, indicating a pipeline of newly started projects alongside many nearing completion. While physical progress exceeds financial progress in the 81–100 per cent range, financial progress is relatively higher in the early stages, reflecting upfront expenditure patterns in project implementation. Ministry of Road Transport & Highways accounts for the highest number of projects, with 993 projects (56 per cent), and a share of total revised project cost of Rs 9.62 lakh crore (26 per cent), highlighting its central role in national infrastructure development. Ministry of Railways is implementing 190 projects (11 per cent), with a total revised project cost of Rs 6.38 lakh crore (17 per cent). Ministry of Coal accounts for implementing 121 projects (7 per cent), with a total revised project cost of Rs 2.22 lakh crore (6 per cent). The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, Ministry of Power, Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs, and the Department of Water Resources, River Development & GR are implementing 103, 98, 50, and 38 projects, with associated revised costs of Rs 4.23 lakh crore, Rs 6.08 lakh crore, Rs 3.78 lakh crore, and Rs 2.01 lakh crore, respectively. The remaining 182 projects (10%), with a total revised cost of Rs 2.78 lakh crore

bihar_raw_news.title: Nepal flash flood: Bihar on high alert over possible Gandak river water level surge
bihar_raw_news.content: PATNA — The Bihar government on Wednesday intensified flood preparedness across districts along the Gandak river following warnings of a possible flash-flood wave in the river's upper catchment area in Nepal. Preliminary assessments indicate that a flood wave of around three metres could potentially reach the Gandak, prompting authorities to place several districts on high alert. A high-level review meeting chaired by Bihar Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit was held on Wednesday, with District Magistrates, senior police officers and Superintendents of Police from vulnerable districts joining via video conference. The meeting reviewed the situation in Nepal and its possible impact on Bihar. The Chief Secretary directed officials to ensure that rescue, evacuation and relief arrangements are completed in advance and that people can be moved to safer locations immediately if river levels rise suddenly. Special vigilance has been ordered in West Champaran (Bettiah), East Champaran (Motihari), Gopalganj, Saran, Muzaffarpur, and Vaishali. Authorities in Sitamarhi and Sheohar, along with other vulnerable districts, have also been instructed to maintain continuous monitoring. Also Read: 17 killed, nearly 500 missing as massive flash flood sweeps through Nepal districts Officials have been directed to regularly inspect river levels, embankments, low-lying areas, bridges, culverts and other vulnerable infrastructure and immediately report any signs of damage or stress. The state has begun pre-deploying additional emergency resources. An NDRF team is being sent to Gopalganj, while another will remain on standby in Muzaffarpur.

bihar_raw_news.title: Gen Alpha rise to demand accountability, better infra - MillenniumPost
bihar_raw_news.content: Gen Alpha rise to demand accountability, better infra By - Team MP Update: 2026-08-26 19:10 GMT New Delhi: The summer of student discontent is moving into autumn... from Jantar Mantar to obscure muddy paths, from the heart of the Indian capital to villages and towns fighting for a place on the education map, and from Gen Z to Gen Alpha. And the sounds of protests are getting ever louder. Picking up from the June-July Cockroach Janta Party-led agitation focusing on alleged corruption in NEET exams, hundreds of much younger school students have taken to the streets to highlight their problems. Bringing up issues such as no fans, no toilets, no teachers and no infrastructure, not even a proper building. Across India’s social and political landscape, Gen Alpha students – those born between 2010 and 2024 -- have taken it upon themselves to improve their learning environments. The reports have come in from Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh with students finding their voice, even in the midst of adverse circumstances, to spotlight problems that are immediate and personal. A major win came last week from a primary school in a village in Rajasthan’s Jaipur where students were attending classes from a cattle enclosure. Following a confrontation between members of the CJP, who wanted to inspect a school in Rampura Kanwarpura village, and some villagers, the state government announced the construction of a new building. The Rampura school building, it admitted, was declared dilapidated in September 2025 and classes were being held in a cattle enclosure. Reacting to the announcement, CJP co-founder and spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the party’s immediate demand over the Rampura school had been addressed, but its campaign on the condition of government schools would continue.

national_raw_news.content: More than 100 Indians are among nearly 500 people reported missing in Nepal after flash floods in the Bhote Koshi River hit the Rasuwa region near the Tibet border this morning. Security officials said that so far, 46 bodies have been recovered from the flash flood hit areas. They said, at least 93 people have been rescued from different parts of the affected areas. According to the Nepal Tourism Board, NTB, the missing people include foreign tourists and Nepali citizens. Officials said, the missing people include at least 105 Indians and 37 NRIs, with most of them headed for the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra in Tibet. They said, missing foreign nationals are from several countries, including United Kingdom, Australia, the United States, Malaysia, South Africa and the Netherlands. The flood reportedly surged through the Bhote Koshi River at around 9 am local time affecting Rasuwa and Dhading districts. It then spread to Dhading, Nuwakot and Chitawan districts, damaging at least four permanent bridges and few temporary ones. Preliminary information suggests that the flash flood was caused by an earthquake triggering an avalanche with melted snow pouring into the Bhote Koshi river. The flash floods in the Bhote Koshi River caused a major disruption in the Rasuwa region, triggering concerns over the safety of tourists and other people present in the affected areas. Authorities and rescue agencies are continuing efforts to assess the situation and establish the whereabouts of those reported missing. The Nepal Tourism Board has also issued emergency contact numbers for tourists and their families seeking information or assistance. The emergency contacts include the toll-free number 1234, the hotline 1144 and the Tourist Police number 9851289445. The tourism board urged tourists in the affected areas to remain calm, stay informed through official channels and follow all safety instructions issued by the authorities. In view of the situation, Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah has consulted with federal parliamentarians from the affected areas. The discussion focused on the damage caused by the flash flood, the condition of coastal settlements, and rescue and relief efforts. Earlier in the day, Mr. Shah had convened a meeting of the National Council for Disaster Risk Reduction and Management to review the situation in the flood-affected areas and the progress of rescue, search and relief efforts. Search and rescue operations are underway, and further details are awaited.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 251 India assures all possible assistance to Nepal for rescue and relief operations
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu has conveyed sympathies to Nepalese President Ramchandra Paudel and the people of Nepal on the devastation caused by the flash floods today. In a social media post, the President expressed solidarity with Nepal at this difficult hour. President Murmu said that India stands ready to support the relief and rescue efforts of the Nepal Government for those affected by this calamity. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan today expressed grief over the loss of lives and devastation caused by the flash floods in Nepal. In a social media post, Mr Radhakrishnan conveyed his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured. He also prayed for the safe and swift rescue of all those who are missing. Mr Radhakrishnan said that the thoughts of the people of India are with the people of Nepal during this difficult hour. Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke to his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah and conveyed condolences on the loss of lives due to the floods in Nepal. In a social media post, Mr Modi said, the people of India stand in solidarity with their sisters and brothers in Nepal at this difficult time. He said, India is ready to provide all possible humanitarian assistance to Nepal. The Prime Minister said, our teams are coordinating closely on rescue and relief efforts. India has dispatched 10 tonnes of Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief and essential medicines to support Nepal which faced devastating floods today. In a social media post, External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar, said that India stands with Nepal and its people in the face of this challenge. He said that his thoughts are with the bereaved families and all those affected by the floods.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | Regional News 125 Bihar and UP step up preparedness amid possible rise in water levels of rivers after flash floods...
national_raw_news.content: Bihar has stepped up flood preparedness following flash floods in Nepal and the possibility of a sudden rise in the water level of the Gandak River. Six districts of the state – West Champaran, East Champaran, Gopalganj, Saran, Muzaffarpur and Vaishali – have been placed under heightened vigilance along the Gandak river system. Besides, District Magistrates of Sitamarhi, Sheohar and other districts have also been directed to keep a close and continuous watch on the situation. People living in low-lying areas of Bagaha in West Champaran and Vaishali district have been urged to move to safer places at the earliest. In view of the possibility of increased water flow in the Gandak River, an NDRF team has been deployed in Gopalganj and Bettiah, while another team has been kept on standby in Muzaffarpur. Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary said that a high-level team has been constituted to closely monitor the situation. In view of the situation, a high-level review meeting was held today in Patna under the chairmanship of Bihar Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit. District Magistrates and senior police officials of the concerned districts have been directed to maintain round-the-clock surveillance and keep rescue and relief arrangements on standby. Union Home Minister Amit Shah also spoke to Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary over the phone in view of the flood threat in Bihar due to torrential rain and glacier burst in Nepal. Home Minister assured the state government of providing all possible assistance to deal with the emerging situation. Mr Shah added that National Disaster Response Force is being mobilised to deal with the situation. In Uttar Pradesh, vigilance has been intensified in the bordering districts of Maharajganj and Kushinagar following severe flooding in the Bhotekoshi River in Nepal’s Rasuwa region. Due to the flooding in Nepal, water levels in the Gandak and Narayani rivers may rise in both districts. Describing the damage caused by the severe flooding in Nepal as deeply concerning, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed the local administration in Maharajganj and Kushinagar to ensure all necessary preparedness measures. CM Yogi Adityanath also instructed the local administration to maintain strict vigilance and closely monitor the rivers’ water levels. He also prayed to Lord Pashupatinath for the safety and well-being of all those affected. The National Disaster Response Force NDRF has deployed nine teams in Bihar and 11 teams in Uttar Pradesh to deal with the emerging situation following the flash floods in Nepal. Talking to media in New Delhi, NDRF Commandant Gyaneshwar Singh said, out of the nine teams in Bihar, two teams have been deployed in Gandak river basin, West Champaran and Muzaffarpur. He said, among the 11 teams in UP one team has been deployed in Kushinagar. Mr Singh said, keeping in view the anticipated floods in the Gandak river due to the flash flood incident in Nepal, NDRF is on high alert.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 39 India and China reaffirm commitment to peace and tranquillity in border areas
national_raw_news.content: India and China have reaffirmed their commitment to maintain peace and tranquility in the border areas and create an atmosphere for healthy and steady development of bilateral relations. The 25th Round of Talks between the Special Representatives (SR) of India and China on the Boundary Question was held in Beijing yesterday. Special Representative of China, Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs Wang Yi and Special Representative of India and National Security Adviser Ajit Doval had a candid and in-depth exchange of views on the India-China boundary question and reached eight points of outcomes and consensus. The two sides underlined their commitment to advancing negotiations on a framework for the settlement of the boundary question. It will be in accordance with the Agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for Settlement of the India-China Boundary Question signed in 2005 and the consensus reached in subsequent SR Talks in pursuit of a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution. The Expert Group on Boundary Delimitation and Working Group on Border Management under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination WMCC would respectively advance discussions on an Early and Substantial Harvest of boundary delimitation and Border Management. The first task for both these groups would be to agree on their respective Terms of Reference. India and China agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly through existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander-level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC. The two sides discussed ways to improve understanding of LAC in appropriate areas, for better border management. With the objective to improve the border management measures, an additional two meeting points were agreed for holding the General Level Mechanism or Senior Highest Military Commander meeting. Similarly two additional channels of border military hotline in the Eastern and Middle Sectors were agreed. Both sides noted the progress on trans-border cooperation. The Indian side appreciated the efforts made by the Chinese side to increase the number of batches of Indian official pilgrimage Kailash-Manasarovar Yatra in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China. Both sides appreciated the reopening of the three designated border trading points. The two sides agreed to strengthen exchanges and cooperation in border trade, pilgrimage and other areas, with the view to work together to create an atmosphere featuring dialogue, peace, consultation and cooperation in the border areas. The two sides also agreed to hold the next meeting of the India-China Expert-Level Mechanism on Trans-border Rivers next month and maintain communication on issues including hydrological data sharing, and renewal of the relevant MoUs. India and China agreed to hold the 26th round of SR Talks in India next year.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | Regional News 372 Festival of Onam being celebrated with traditional fervour
national_raw_news.content: Keralites across the globe are celebrating Thiru Onam today. Akashvani correspondent reports that Thiru Onam celebrations began with Ona Pookkalam, the traditional floral carpet made to welcome the legendary King Mahabali. This harvest festival is celebrated by Keralites irrespective of caste and religion. Special poojas are being held at temples, including the hill shrine of Sabarimala, Aranmula and Guruvayur. Ona Sadya, the traditional Kerala feast, is another major attraction of Thiru Onam. Thousands of cultural programmes and traditional games will be held across Keralam this afternoon, including official celebrations. Heavy rush is being experienced at temples across the state, despite the rain. President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings and best wishes to all citizens, especially the people of Keralam living in India and abroad. In her message, President Murmu noted that Onam is an occasion to express gratitude to nature on the arrival of the new harvest. She added that the festival celebrates India’s rich culture and spirit of brotherhood, promoting unity in diversity. The President mentioned that Boat races, folk dances, music and sports are important traditions associated with this festival, which showcase the culture and values of Keralam. President Murmu prayed that this auspicious festival brings happiness, peace, good health and prosperity to all and inspires the citizens to contribute to the nation’s progress. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan has extended greetings to everyone on the occasion of Onam. Sharing a social media post, the Vice President prayed that this cherished festival, which reflects Keralam’s rich cultural heritage and timeless traditions, fill every home with happiness, good health and prosperity. Mr Radhakrishnan wished that the spirit of Onam strengthen harmony, unity and hope in society. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also extended greetings to the countrymen on the occasion of Onam. Sharing a social media post, the Prime Minister said that the vibrant festival is celebrated all over the world with great enthusiasm. Mr Modi wished that this festival further empowers the spirit of happiness, togetherness, and prosperity. Home Minister Amit Shah has extended greetings to the people of Keralam on the occasion of Onam. Sharing a social media post, Mr Shah prayed that this joyous occasion usher in a year filled with peace, prosperity and well-being for all.

national_raw_news.title: Haryana CM Nayab Singh Saini honours Commonwealth Games medalists and participants 54 mins ago 24
national_raw_news.content: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini honoured Commonwealth Games medallists and participants from Haryana at a state-level felicitation ceremony held in Panchkula today. Cash awards totalling ₹13 crore 97 lakh 50 thousand were presented to 24 athletes at the event. Expressing pride in the athletes’ achievements, the Chief Minister remarked that an athlete’s success is underpinned by the faith of their parents, the discipline instilled by their mentors, and the resolve to rise again after every defeat. He noted that India secured the fourth position on the medal tally at the 23rd Commonwealth Games, winning a total of 39 medals comprising 13 gold, 17 silver, and 9 bronze. Haryana once again distinguished itself during this glorious moment. He highlighted that while Haryana accounts for merely 2 percent of the country’s total population, athletes from the state clinched a total of 11 medals in these games. Commending the performance of the state’s daughters in particular, the Chief Minister pointed out that 6 of the 11 medals won by Haryana’s athletes were secured by women, including 5 gold medals. He expressed confidence that, driven by the prowess of its athletes, India would emerge as a global sporting powerhouse at the Olympic Games.
